The missed scope is bounded outcomes. Sudijono–Dobriban–Tchetgen’s binary theorem uses the same unrestricted design/estimator class, while their Theorem 2.3 proves exact endpoint reduction for outcomes in any common interval \([L,U]\) ([Theorems 2.2–2.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.13822)). The identical argument works for this zero-sum three-arm contrast:

- Endpoint schedules \(Y_i(a)\in\{L,U\}\) are a subset of \([L,U]^{3n}\), so inclusion transfers every binary converse.
- Conversely, normalize \(S_i(a)=(Y_i(a)-L)/(U-L)\), independently Bernoulliize the normalized complete schedule, apply the binary procedure, and Rao–Blackwellize over the auxiliary Bernoulli variables conditional on observed normalized outcomes. Jensen’s inequality transfers the binary upper bound for every unrestricted design and every fixed iid \(q\).
- Because \(\sum_a c_a=0\), the target scales without an offset. Thus, exactly at every finite \(n\),
  \[
  \rho^{\mathrm{all}}_{n,[L,U]}=(U-L)^2\rho^{\mathrm{all}}_{n,\mathrm{bin}},\qquad
  \rho^{\mathrm{iid}}_{n,[L,U]}(q)=(U-L)^2\rho^{\mathrm{iid}}_{n,\mathrm{bin}}(q).
  \]
  The sharp constant, allocation frontier, and matching constructions therefore transfer wholesale, multiplied by \((U-L)^2\). The eight-type orbit game should be described as representing the bounded game’s endpoint minimax value, not as a literal orbit reduction of continuous schedules.
